parts:
Hello,

How can I reproduce the same graph exactly using ggplot2? The example graph is located in slide 7 (end) of the PDF:
http://www.inf.ethz.ch/personal/markusp/teaching/263-2300-ETH-spring12/slides/benchmarking.pdf

There is specified all the requirements in detail. I believe that the plot shown in the slides is produced using MS excel but I was wondering if I can get exactly the same using ggplot2 ... using the default ggplot2 doesn't seem to be too far off but I wonder what options I shall use to get exactly the same?

Many thanks in advance,
Best regards,
Giovanni

messages.author: d31339b95f6e694c
messages.subject: Re: how to reproduce exactly this plot with ggplot2?
parts:
On 2012-Apr-04, at 20:56 , Giovanni Azua wrote:
>
>
> How can I reproduce the same graph exactly using ggplot2? The example graph is located in slide 7 (end) of the PDF:
> http://www.inf.ethz.ch/personal/markusp/teaching/263-2300-ETH-spring12/slides/benchmarking.pdf
>
> There is specified all the requirements in detail. I believe that the plot shown in the slides is produced using MS excel but I was wondering if I can get exactly the same using ggplot2 ... using the default ggplot2 doesn't seem to be too far off but I wonder what options I shall use to get exactly the same?

A completely exact reproduction is impossible I think. Here is the closest I can get to it (and there is a lot of messing around involved):

# generate somewhat similar data
set.seed(123)
d <- data.frame(
n=4:13,
value=rep(c(5,3,2,1), each=10) + rnorm(10*4),
kind=rep(c("Spiral SSE", "Intel MKL", "Spiral vectorized", "Spiral scalar"), each=10),
main=c(rep(TRUE, times=10), rep(FALSE, times=30))
)
# reorder the levels of the "kind" column
d$kind <- factor(d$kind, levels=c("Spiral SSE", "Intel MKL", "Spiral vectorized", "Spiral scalar"))

library("ggplot2")
library("directlabels")

p <- ggplot(data=d, mapping=aes(x=n, y=value, colour=kind)) +
# basic geoms for the non main line
geom_path() + geom_point() +
# choose colours manually
scale_colour_manual(values=c("red", "darkblue", "grey20", "grey40"), guide="none") +
# overlay the main data with thicker line and larger points
# NB: we cannot map size to main because we cannot control separately the size of the line and the size of the points
geom_path(data=d[d$main,], size=1, colour="red") + geom_point(data=d[d$main,], size=3, colour="red") +
# fake x axis
geom_hline(aes(yintercept=0)) +
# rename y axis and adjust its limits and breaks manually (should do this based on the data)
scale_y_continuous("[Gflop/s]", limit=c(0,7), breaks=1:6, expand=c(0,0)) +
# remove horizontal padding on x axis and break at every n
scale_x_continuous(expand=c(0,0), breaks=seq(min(d$n), max(d$n), by=1)) +
opts(
# use the plot title as the y axis main title
title="DFT 2n (single precision) on Pentium 4, 2.53 GHz\n",
# NB: cannot make the n exponent because using expression here prevents text bolding and the new line in the end which allows to put the y axis label as a second line
# make it bold and left aligned
plot.title=theme_text(hjust=0, face="bold"),
# reposition the y axis title (which us just the units here)
axis.title.y=theme_text(angle=0, vjust=1.08, hjust=10),
# decrease left side margin to compensate for the modification of the y title position
plot.margin=unit(c(1,1,0.5,-2), "lines"),
# remove minor grid lines
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank(),
# draw ticks and axis labels in black
axis.ticks=theme_segment(),
axis.text.x=theme_text(),
axis.text.y=theme_text()#,
# add axis line
# NB: fails due to a bug
# axis.line=theme_line(colour="black", size=0.5)

# NB: cannot selectively remove vertical grid lines, ticks of the y axis, or only draw the x axis (as a true axis), while keeping rest
)
# add line labels directly
p <- direct.label(p, smart.grid)
# remove clipping of start and end points
gt <- ggplot_gtable(ggplot_build(p))
gt$layout$clip[gt$layout$name=="panel"] <- "off"
# draw the plot
grid.draw(gt)


If you don't need the exact visual output, I would personally prefer this:

p <- ggplot(data=d, mapping=aes(x=n, y=value, colour=kind)) +
geom_path(aes(size=main)) + geom_point() +
scale_size_discrete(range=c(0.5,1), guide="none") +
scale_y_continuous("Gflop/s") +
xlim(min(d$n), max(d$n)+2) +
opts(
title="DFT 2n (single precision) on Pentium 4, 2.53 GHz",
plot.title=theme_text(hjust=0.5, face="bold"),
panel.grid.minor=theme_blank()
)
# add line labels directly
p <- direct.label(p, list("last.qp", hjust=-0.1))
p

which is much more regular ggplot syntax and is just as readable and efficient.
